relations.subject: tool:sync-gateway
relations.evidence: Sync Gateway uses GSI (Global Secondary Indexes) and SQL++ to perform a variety of internal operations, including authentication and replication.

relations.subject: sgw:index-num-replicas-setting
relations.evidence: Sync Gateway requires the Index Service to be running on at least two Couchbase Server nodes (required for index replica).

relations.subject: sgw:use-views-setting
relations.evidence: Users wanting to run Sync Gateway 2.1 with an older version of Couchbase Server will need to continue to use views, by setting the `use_views` property.

notable_absence.finding: The page states index.num_replicas CAN be set to zero to run with a single Index Service node ('users can run with a single Index Service node by setting Sync Gateway's `index.num_replicas` property to zero') but never states what the DEFAULT value actually is - only that using zero increases failover downtime risk. No default is recorded here for lack of textual evidence.

cross_component_finding: This very short page (68 lines) functions almost entirely as a hub: its only two substantive paragraphs each end in a cross-reference (to Partitioned Indexes, and by omission of detail, implicitly to the configuration schema reference for the two named properties) rather than explaining the GSI-vs-Views tradeoff in any depth itself. The one-sentence Enterprise/downtime benefit claim ('reduce the downtime ... from several hours to a few seconds') is asserted without the mechanism being explained on this page at all.
cross_product_finding: GSI is reused here as literally the same registry concept (index-type:gsi) that the Couchbase Server Query-service reference tree already promoted, without any Sync-Gateway-specific variant or wrapper concept - Sync Gateway is a straightforward CONSUMER of Couchbase Server's own index type, not a product with its own parallel indexing technology. This is a clean, uncomplicated reuse case, worth contrasting with the more fraught fts:index-partitioning/sgw:index-partitioning near-duplicate flagged in index-partitions.json.
